headline: Grasslands Entry Fees and Backcountry Registration
reservation: All visitors must possess a valid Parks Canada Discovery Pass or daily entry permit, obtainable at the West Block or East Block visitor centers. While front-country camping is booked through the national reservation system, backcountry users must register on-site to ensure safety in this remote prairie landscape.

days.title: West Block Valleys and Wildlife

stops.name: Ecotour Scenic Drive
stops.detail: Drive through the Frenchman River Valley to spot black-tailed prairie dog colonies and grazing bison.

stops.name: Top Dogtown
stops.detail: Walk the short loop to observe the complex social structures of the park's most famous rodent residents.

days.driving: Allow 2–3 hours for the slow-paced loop; conditions vary.
days.note: Bison have the right of way; maintain a safe distance and remain in your vehicle if they are on the road.

days.title: High Viewpoints and Hidden Coulees

stops.name: 70 Mile Butte
stops.detail: Climb the steepest trail in the park for a panoramic view of the vast mixed-grass prairie landscape.

stops.name: Eagle Butte
stops.detail: Explore the higher elevations where raptors frequently soar on the thermal currents.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for trailhead transfers; conditions vary.
days.note: Summer heat can be extreme by midday; aim to complete higher elevation hikes before noon.

days.title: East Block Badlands

stops.name: Badlands Parkway
stops.detail: Traverse the crest of the Rock Creek valley for views of the dramatic, eroded formations of the Killdeer Badlands.

stops.name: Valley of 1,000 Devils
stops.detail: Hike into the rugged terrain where fossils lie embedded in the ancient, exposed layers of the earth.

days.driving: Allow 3–4 hours for transit between blocks and viewpoints; conditions vary.
days.note: The East and West blocks are not connected by internal park roads; allow significant time for the gravel bypass.

intel.title: Trailhead Turnouts
intel.text: Parking is limited to small gravel turnouts at major trailheads like 70 Mile Butte. Large RVs may find maneuvering difficult in the smaller East Block lookouts.

intel.title: Dark Sky Seclusion
intel.text: Cellular service is non-existent in most of the park and unreliable in Val Marie. Carry a physical map and consider a satellite messenger for backcountry trekking.

intel.title: Val Marie Services
intel.text: Val Marie is the primary gateway for the West Block, but fuel hours are restricted. Ensure you have a full tank before attempting the Badlands Parkway in the East Block.

intel.title: Seasonal Heat and Mud
intel.text: Rain can turn prairie ‘gumbo’ roads impassable instantly; check weather forecasts at the visitor center. Peak bloom for wildflowers typically occurs in late June.

intel.title: Remote Road Conditions
intel.text: Many park roads are gravel or dirt; accessibility depends heavily on recent precipitation. The Badlands Parkway is paved but other scenic routes are rugged.

plan.arrival: Pick up a vehicle in Medicine Hat or Swift Current; stock up on water and high-clearance supplies before heading south to Val Marie.
plan.vehicle: A high-clearance vehicle is strongly recommended for the West Block Ecotour and mandatory for some East Block access roads; check rental terms for gravel road usage.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset from the Belza Lookout or 70 Mile Butte offers the best light over the Frenchman River Valley.
